summary: Remote Smokies peak. Tennessee Landforms lists a lookout tower here as historical; a hiking guide describes no tower or summit trail today.

facts.status_note: Tennessee Landforms lists the tower as historical, and a hiking guide describes no observation tower on the summit.

access.note: Reached on the Appalachian Trail across the south slope; the summit itself needs off-trail travel.

visit.trail_note: The Appalachian Trail crosses the south slope; no maintained summit trail.

evidence.quote: the second-highest in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park

evidence.supports: On the Tennessee-North Carolina border, Sevier and Haywood counties
evidence.quote: Mount Guyot lies on the Tennessee-North Carolina border, between Sevier County and Haywood County

evidence.supports: Two peaks; the southwestern one in Tennessee is the true summit
evidence.quote: There are two peaks atop the mountain approximately one-half mile apart, with the southwestern peak in Tennessee being the true summit.

evidence.supports: Landforms table lists Mount Guyot as historical
evidence.quote: Mount Guyot 6621' Sevier FB2486 gsmnp historical

evidence.supports: Park's Tennessee-side lookout list includes Guyot as current or former
evidence.quote: Lookout towers (or former locations) on the Tennessee side of the Great Smoky Mountain National Park

evidence.supports: Guyot is not marked standing; Mount Cammerer is
No road, observation tower, maintained summit trail or panoramic platform drawing crowds
evidence.quote: there is no road, observation tower, maintained summit trail, or panoramic platform drawing crowds to its top

evidence.supports: Appalachian Trail crosses the south slope, within 1,000 ft of the summit
evidence.quote: While the mountain is remote, the Appalachian Trail crosses its south slope, passing to within 1,000 feet (300 m) of the summit.

evidence.supports: Reaching the high point requires off-trail travel through dense forest
evidence.quote: Reaching the high point requires leaving the maintained trail and navigating through extremely dense high-elevation spruce-fir forest.

evidence.supports: Most visitors are better served hiking the Appalachian Trail across the slopes
evidence.quote: For most visitors, the better experience is simply hiking the Appalachian Trail across Guyot’s slopes

notes_for_editor: No build date, staffing or fire history found for the Guyot tower; the only tower-specific statement is the Tennessee Landforms 'historical' mark. The Upland Chronicles article ('Few Fire Towers remain in Smokies', Mountain Press) is the likeliest source for the tower's history but returned HTTP 429 twice and was not read. Read budget for this tower ran over the guide's limit of 6 (about 7 page reads, one of them the shared landforms page). Agency is inferred from the park listing on the Tennessee Landforms page. The brief's NGS id FB 2486 appears in Tennessee Landforms as the Guyot waypoint code and in Wikipedia as the NGS datasheet for the summit; it may be a survey mark rather than a tower registration, so a human should check. Elevation: the Mountain Field Guide gives a LiDAR figure of 6,623.9 ft; the record's 2018.1 m matches the NPS 6,621 ft figure, so no correction is proposed. The Cabins USA Gatlinburg Smokies tower guide lists six towers and not Guyot; it was not used.
